scope: Complete source-only classification of template.md, not fulfillment or a review of externally linked legal/RFC documents. Related primary atoms are cross-references, not inherited assessments or evidence. Future-author and unimplemented-extension conditions remain explicit.

coverage.reason: Generated-file banner, protocol introduction, license/trademark notices and warranty disclaimer. Links to external license/scope/trademark texts are not a product legal clearance.
Illustrative Mermaid flow, not an alternative normative state machine or an additional role/message implementation obligation.
Definitions, credential generation, identity and session classification.
Role versions, namespace, priority and activation responsibilities.
Server skew tracking and its connection-phase limitation.
Conditional custom-role names, versions and binary-ID rules.
Versioning, optional information, capability confirmation and connection-wide extension contracts.
Template include directives. Nine selected documents have the primary inventory; source capture remains an explicitly unoffered role, not silently implemented.

clauses.statement: Apply BCP 14 special keyword force only to uppercase words.
clauses.notes: Declarative field/sequence contracts still matter; lowercase guidance is not automatically an uppercase SHOULD.

clauses.condition: Identifying protocol actors, roles, groups and streams
clauses.statement: Keep server orchestration, client roles, one-group membership and client-specific role streams distinct.
clauses.notes: Definitions do not add source capture or a server to this SDK. Per-client encoding/group construction remains server-owned.

clauses.statement: Draw the identity private key from an adequately seeded CSPRNG.
clauses.notes: Existing primary generation-source and distinct-device tests were reviewed for this same predicate; no statistical entropy certification.

clauses.statement: Use the unpadded 43-character Base64URL Curve25519 public key as the persistent identifier.
clauses.notes: The SDK Store owns persistence; a shared Store path is not a way to create another independent device.

clauses.condition: Generating a new long-term pairing secret
clauses.statement: Generate a 32-byte long-term PSK from a CSPRNG.
clauses.notes: Additional generation-source predicate: session.activate uses crypto/rand.Read, independently guarded by TestLongTermPairingSecretGenerationUsesCSPRNG. Related length/binding rows alone do not prove randomness; this inventory does not inherit their T.

clauses.statement: Generate the per-device 32-byte pairing PSK from a CSPRNG.
clauses.notes: Distinct from both the long-term pairing result and public Sentinel constant.

clauses.condition: Exposing the pairing secret to an operator
clauses.statement: Distribute the pairing PSK together with the client identity in a pairing token.
clauses.notes: The standalone token encoder is not a printed QR label.

clauses.condition: A product selects a pairing-code method
clauses.statement: Distinguish fixed eight-digit static codes from per-session dynamic digits or QR payloads.
clauses.notes: Neither code method is offered by the SDK; this definition does not turn one into a mandatory feature.

clauses.statement: Restore provisioned credentials/settings and clear accumulated state including pairing records.
clauses.notes: No Factory Reset API is offered. Erasing a file and generating a new identity is not represented as restoring factory-provisioned identity/delay.

clauses.statement: Treat only a long-term-PSK session as paired; pairing/Sentinel sessions remain unpaired.
clauses.notes: Derived locally, not an extra wire field or an authentication claim for Sentinel.

clauses.statement: Use an explicit role@version identifier.
clauses.notes: Current supported role families each implement v1 only.

clauses.statement: Implement all versions of all roles described by this specification.
clauses.notes: Server obligation; receiver tests do not certify it.

clauses.condition: Defining or advertising a new role name/version
clauses.statement: Do not appropriate standard names or versions reserved for future revisions.
clauses.notes: Config rejects unknown/custom names rather than offering an unchecked extension path.

clauses.statement: Preserve most-preferred-first ordering.
clauses.notes: Config copies the ordered role list; exact hello inventories assert outgoing order.

clauses.condition: Implementing multiple versions of the same role
clauses.statement: List all supported versions.
clauses.notes: Current SDK implements only v1. A future version addition must reopen this conditional recommendation.

clauses.statement: Select at most one version per family, using the first implemented offered match or none by policy.
clauses.notes: Server selection algorithm, separate from client duplicate/unoffered-role rejection.

clauses.statement: Do not activate an unoffered role/version.
clauses.notes: The client validates received activation; it does not implement the server.

clauses.statement: Consult received activation state before emitting role-specific data.
clauses.notes: Supported does not mean active.

clauses.statement: Use unversioned object keys within the selected role-version contract.
clauses.notes: Do not infer role-v2 support from a player key.

clauses.statement: Track role-version skew as an operator update signal.
clauses.notes: Server diagnostics, not a new client wire field.

clauses.statement: Role skew detection cannot diagnose a core/suite/handshake mismatch before roles are exchanged.
clauses.notes: Current core version remains exactly 1.

clauses.condition: Advertising an application-specific role in a future supported extension profile
clauses.statement: Prefix the role with underscore and include an explicit version.
clauses.notes: Current Config rejects all unimplemented roles, including underscore-prefixed names. No extension implementation or future grammar is claimed.

clauses.statement: Include a vendor-specific prefix to avoid collisions.
clauses.notes: Conditional product/extension naming guidance; not a new SDK role API.

clauses.condition: Defining a future application-specific binary role
clauses.statement: Allocate its IDs from unmanaged 192-255 and define the assignment in that role.
clauses.notes: No application-specific binary IDs are advertised or dispatched by this SDK profile.

clauses.statement: Do not advertise conflicting binary IDs.
clauses.notes: Current unknown/custom-role configuration is rejected, not accepted without collision checks.

clauses.condition: Adding an unselected future protocol feature
clauses.statement: Leave existing behavior unchanged when that feature is not selected.
clauses.notes: Protocol-author responsibility and receiver compatibility boundary, not permission for this SDK to invent negotiated behavior.

clauses.statement: Assign a new role version.
clauses.notes: No new role version is introduced by this work.

clauses.statement: Assign a new core version unless the change applies only with explicit bilateral opt-in.
clauses.notes: Spec release, core version and role version remain separate.

clauses.statement: Add information older receivers can ignore without changing meaning.
clauses.notes: Permission for a future specification revision, not permission to emit arbitrary fields now.

clauses.statement: Confirm support through activation or explicit capability negotiation first.
clauses.notes: Neither matching core nor software version nor no-error is sufficient confirmation.

clauses.statement: Use role support objects.
clauses.notes: Current mandatory support objects stay exact; no speculative capability field is added.

clauses.statement: Define bilateral opt-in and the no-opt-in outcome.
clauses.notes: Admission/ownership changes cannot be smuggled through an unrelated role.

clauses.statement: Do not break the rules for nonparticipating peer connections.
clauses.notes: A future extension needs its own multi-connection compatibility review.

clauses.condition: Inferring a connection-wide capability from role support
clauses.statement: Do not infer it unless that role version explicitly includes it.
clauses.notes: No such optional connection-wide behavior is offered by the current profile.
